Subject: Scalable crediting & incremental commit structure for new product workloads

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, I attached a concise proposal and a small calculator showing how incremental commits map to per-token economics across workloads (generation vs embeddings). Highlights:

- Baseline hosted per-token rate (on our standard Gen M profile): $0.00060 per token.
- Tiered commit discounts: 10% at $50k/month equivalent, 18% at $150k/month, 25% at $400k/month (these are illustrative, final bands flexible).
- Incremental commit structure: new workloads (product launches / new teams) can be added as "incremental commits" that receive a blended discount based on the additional commit only — i.e., you don’t lose your prior effective rate for existing workloads. This avoids a major upfront re-commit across teams.
- Embeddings SKU priced separately (typically ~40% of text gen unit cost) with its own commit banding.
- Unused committed credits: 60-day roll-forward by default; annual true-up.
- Pilot mechanism: we can do a 3-month pilot commit ($50k) to validate cost and QPS, then convert to a longer commit with a ramped discount.

I attached: nebula_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal summary) and commit_calculator.xlsx (quick model).

Would you be available for a 30-minute call this week to walk through the calculator with your usage profile? Proposed slots: Wed 11/3 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 11/4 13:00-13:30 PT.

Best,

Thanks, the materials are helpful. A few quick clarifying questions before we set the call:

1) Our immediate ask: new product "Patient Summaries" (generation-heavy) is projected at ~500M tokens/month in Q1 post-launch. How does the incremental-commit math work if we add that workload mid-contract? Will all tokens for that product be treated under the incremental band, or is there a blended retro rate?

2) We have an embeddings-heavy analytics pipeline (team B). Do embeddings commits pool with generation commits or are they separate credits? If separate, can we get a combined discount when both are committed?

3) Rollover: 60-day roll-forward is workable — can we get a 90-day option at the next tier?

4) Term & termination: if we do a pilot-to-commit path, how do we prevent double-charging if the pilot spend is then converted to a longer commit?

Also attaching our internal usage estimates for both workloads (nebula_usage_estimates.csv) so you have concrete numbers.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Scalable crediting & incremental commit structure for new product workloads

Elena —

Thanks for the details and the file — that helps. Short answers up front, then proposed concrete structure: 

1) Patient Summaries (500M tokens/month): if you add this workload mid-contract as an incremental commit, all tokens for that product are accounted under the incremental commit bucket going forward (no retroactive re-rate for past usage). We do offer a one-time true-up credit during conversion windows to smooth the transition; for example, if you convert a 3-month pilot into a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, we apply pilot spend as an advanced credit against the first invoice so you’re not double-charged.

2) Embeddings vs generation: we treat them as separate SKUs for metering. However, we support a blended discount when customers commit to both in a single agreement — typically we calculate a weighted blended rate based on forecasted token mix. In practice that often yields ~2-6ppt additional discount compared to separate commitments.

3) Rollovers: 60 days standard; 90 days available at the $150k+/month equivalent tier (or by contract amendment).

4) Pilot -> commit path: pilot spend applied as a credit (see #1). We’ll document the conversion window in the SOW; short version — pilot credit applied, remainder converted to committed credit balance.

Concrete proposal (to consider on our call):
- Pilot: $50k upfront credit for 3 months, covers the first X tokens (calculator attached shows exact mapping).
- Conversion: if you convert within 30 days, we apply the $50k as a pre-paid against the annual commit and then set the monthly billing to the committed rate (with the discount band applicable to the additional commit only).
- New workload accelerator: first 90 days after launch we offer a 10% temporary uplift credit (effectively additional discount) on incremental tokens for the product to offset early-stage cost risk.
- SLA / availability: Standard SLA included; Financial SLA credits negotiable at higher commit tiers. Vivek — will flag to finance for approval if we need a monetary SLA credit.

If that sounds reasonable, propose Wed 11/3 10:00 PT to walk through the calculator. Lauren and Vivek will join to finalize bands if we move toward a signed SOW.

Best,
Rishi
